front.title: User-Controlled Device Authorization for MLS using did:webvh Credentials

abstract.t:
In Messaging Layer Security (MLS), whoever operates the Authentication Service (AS) decides which devices belong to a user. When providers federate MLS groups, as the More Instant Messaging Interoperability (MIMI) work does, every member of a group must accept devices vouched for by every other member's provider. Any one provider can therefore add a device under one of its users' names to any group that user is in. Other members cannot prevent this; at best they detect it after the device has joined.
This document defines an MLS credential type in which the user, not the provider, authorizes each device. The credential carries the user's did:webvh log: a hash-chained, signed history of the user's device keys that any member can verify offline. It also defines group rules that make every member reach the same validity decision and that propagate device revocation through ordinary Commits.
